key_insight: This study shows that AI adoption in Nigerian healthcare is constrained less by the technology itself and more by workforce readiness, including awareness, preparedness, and confidence to use AI in clinical settings. It highlights that successful clinical AI deployment in LMICs requires targeted training and implementation support, not just tool availability.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between rapid AI development and the real-world readiness of healthcare workers to safely and effectively adopt AI in Nigeria, where training, infrastructure, and institutional support may be limited.
method: Cross-sectional survey of 761 healthcare professionals across multiple disciplines and practice settings in Nigeria
Assessment of awareness, attitudes, preparedness, and perceived barriers to clinical AI adoption
Analysis of workforce readiness patterns to identify key implementation challenges and training needs
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this emphasizes that model performance alone is not enough for deployment in healthcare; adoption depends on user trust, education, and workflow fit. The findings can guide more responsible AI implementation strategies in LMIC health systems.
visual_elements: A readiness gauge or scorecard showing awareness, attitude, preparedness, and barriers
A stacked bar chart comparing AI readiness across professional groups and practice settings
An icon-based barrier map highlighting training, infrastructure, and policy challenges
A workflow diagram showing the path from AI development to clinical adoption
paper_title: Prepared Or Unprepared? Evaluating Healthcare Workforce Readiness for Clinical Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria
paper_authors: Abbas M. Rabiu, Abdulrazaq A. Zubair, Um-mulkhairi Ibrahim, Tolulope Olusuyi, Shaheeda Farouq
